title: SLI fidelity and granular error-budget brokering protocol for endpoints and model variants
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define a reproducible SLI/SLO and error-budget broker framework that (1) produces per-endpoint and per-model-variant SLIs with consistent fidelity across regions, (2) supports a ledger-based error-budget accounting system for borrowing and reclaiming budget across routes and tenants, and (3) exposes deterministic brokering rules used by circuit-breakers and load-shedding logic during multi-region failover. This ticket covers measurement definitions, aggregation windows, telemetry tag schema, burn-rate alerting thresholds, and the API surface for the broker to query/claim budgets at decision time.

acceptance_criteria: Canonical SLI definitions committed to runtime-1.20 docs (latency: token-normalized p95; availability: 99.9% success rate; quality: promptset pass-rate >= threshold).
Error-budget ledger implemented: transactions (debit/credit/lease/reclaim) and exports available; ledgers persisted for 90 days and queryable over API.
Brokering API implemented with deterministic priority rules and unit tests (prefer pinned variant, tenant reservation, regional preference).
Circuit-breaker and load-shedding modules wire up to brokering decisions and enact pre-approved eviction policies in a test cluster.
Console shows per-route error-budget state and burn-rate alerts; alert thresholds wired to PagerDuty playbook.
decisions: Measure latency as token-normalized p95 for request lifecycle (ingress -> first token -> completion) to account for variable output size.
Availability SLI defined as percentage of requests returning 2xx status and non-empty response within configured timeout window.
Quality SLO is evaluated separately via scheduled promptset evaluations; acceptance is a pass-rate over the promptset per model-version and route.
Error-budget ledger model: each route has a daily budget quota; budgets may be leased to other routes via broker with priority weights and expiry timestamps.
Brokering policy: prefer intra-tenant borrowing, then sibling-route borrowing, then cross-tenant (lowest priority); global admin can grant emergency overrides.
Circuit-breaker thresholds based on short-window burn-rate (>4x baseline over 5m) triggers staged shedding: soft-throttle -> variant-eviction -> region-failover.
For multi-region incident handling, routing will prefer regional spare capacity first; only when regional failover exceeds reclaimable budget will cross-region routing happen.
steps: 1) Finalize telemetry schema (tags: tenant_id, route, model_version, variant, region, request_type, token_count).
2) Implement SLI calculations in metrics pipeline with token-normalized latency and per-request quality markers.
3) Build error-budget ledger service (REST API + durable store) and integrate with existing quota service.
4) Implement deterministic brokering algorithm and expose endpoints: /broker/claim, /broker/release, /broker/status.
5) Wire brokering decisions into runtime circuit-breaker and load-shed hooks with feature flags.
6) Add Console panels and burn-rate alerts; create runbook steps and PagerDuty escalation paths.
7) Run canary with synthetic traffic, fault-injection, and tenant-simulated bursts; iterate on thresholds.
proposed_rollout: Feature-flag broker API for internal testing in staging (runtime-staging) week 1.
Enable canary on a small set of low-traffic routes with canary window 72h; observe burn-rate and false positive rate.
Stage to two regions with soft-throttle only for 7 days, collect metrics and tenant feedback.
Full rollout gated by quality SLO stability and successful tenant dry-run; automatic rollback if burn-rate > 6x baseline for 30m.
test_plan: Unit tests for ledger transaction semantics (idempotency, TTL expiry, concurrency).
Integration tests for broker API with simulated concurrent claims and priority arbitration.
Load tests: synthetic burst scenarios to validate staged-shedding ordering and latency impact.
Chaos test: region ejection simulation confirming broker-enabled graceful eviction before hard-failover.
Quality validation: run promptset against canary model-variants pre- and post-brokering to confirm no regression.
notes: We intentionally separate quality SLOs from availability/latency so that model rollouts do not incorrectly consume network error budgets.
Token-normalized latency requires adding token_count to every trace and metric; this will slightly increase metric cardinality and storage—plan to roll forward retention adjustments.
Dedicated customers can opt into stricter per-tenant reservation rules; default broker policy applies to public/hosted tenants.
Follow-up work will define billing implications for cross-tenant borrowing (legal & contract considerations).
